conflicts.what: the natural fix for T1 (strip or reject every '&', or reject quotes or '>') changes or rejects legitimate restream commands whose quoted m3u8 and destination URLs contain '&' (restreamer.json.php:604-605,660,677) and that end with ' > log 2>&1' (restreamer.json.php:720), and rejects conversion commands with single-quoted paths (functionsFFMPEG.php:498-499)
a blanket rejection of '$' or backslash is safe for the generated commands, but rejecting or stripping quote characters to stop sh -c breakout breaks the quoted URLs and paths that T6 must preserve

fairness_risks: A '&' that is inside a double-quoted URL in a legitimate ffmpegCommand (restream m3u8 query string, restreamer.json.php:604-605,660) has to survive, but a single-'&' rule written as a plain character ban removes it. A test that requires both needs a quote-aware sanitizer or a token-level allowlist, and the report does not ask for that.

A legitimate restream command arrives with a trailing ' > logfile 2>&1 ' (restreamer.json.php:720). A sanitizer that rejects any '>' or '&' instead of stripping the redirect tail (functions.php:69) would refuse it, so tests should check stripping, not rejection.
notifyCode and callback are base64 (objects/functions.php:3238), so they contain '+', '/' and '='. An alphanumeric allowlist for T3 would break the notify callback; escapeshellarg does not.
Restreamer users_id is 'web', 'commandline' or a numeric id (restreamer.json.php:298,304), so a [A-Za-z0-9_-] allowlist or escapeshellarg on the log path keeps legitimate use working.

design.why: There are four independent fix sites: the sanitizer (functions.php:59-82), the notify concatenation (ffmpeg.json.php:411), the grep keyword (functions.php:109 or ffmpeg.json.php:221/341), and the restreamer log path (restreamer.json.php:318/720/723). Each has a different reason to dismiss: the report covers the sanitizer; the notify values look like trusted ciphertext; keyword appears already sanitized; the log path is in another plugin and looks neutralised on the remote route. T3, T4 and T5 are deepseek-type (protection absent or bypassed, with a strong reason to dismiss). The mimo dimension sits inside the sanitizer group: T2 (sh -c double-quote expansion shapes) and the T6 coupled values ('&' in quoted URLs, the redirect tail, quoted paths) punish over-hardening. That puts both model weaknesses in one checkout while keeping each fix small. T5 is the main risk: it is outside the reported file and its reachability depends on a valid streamer token, so if the design must stay closer to the report, drop T5 and keep T1+T2(+T6 tests), T3 and T4 as a 3-group design.

unverified: Contents of fix A (25c8ab90269e) and fix B (c1cfa2bea8a3) were not inspected (no git access in this run). b_in_code_a_wrote is likely true, since the '&&' removal and the [;|`<>] blacklist at functions.php:65,70 look like A's work, but this is not confirmed.

Whether upstream fix B also escaped notifyCode/callback (T3), the list/isKeywordRunning keyword (T4) or the restreamer log path (T5) is unknown; any of them may already be covered by B's hidden tests or be out of B's scope.

How an attacker obtains a validly encrypted, fresh (30 s) codeToExecEncrypted payload is not established from this checkout; the payload is decrypted by the main site (functions.php:13-31) and ffmpeg.json.php does not check APISecret despite its header comment (ffmpeg.json.php:11-14 vs 120-127). T1-T4 all share this precondition.

T5 reachability: requires a token accepted by plugin/Live/verifyToken.json.php (restreamer.json.php:337-363); whether a low-privilege streamer can obtain one, and whether execFFMPEGAsyncOrRemote is defined after functionsStandAlone.php loads (which decides between line 720 and line 723), was not verified.
Whether PHP parse_url returns a host containing '&' for destination URLs (restreamer.json.php:406) was not verified.
